text: {"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "Fixed get_range() in lib/cmdline.c to advance the output pointer forward (*pint++) instead of backward (*pint--) when expanding a hyphenated range, so subsequent range values land in the correct ints[] slots."}

patch:
diff --git c/lib/kstrtox.c w/lib/kstrtox.c

text: {"changed_files": ["lib/kstrtox.c"], "summary": "Fixed the digit-validity check in _parse_integer_limit from 'val > base' to 'val >= base', so 'a' is no longer accepted as a decimal digit (which made \"5-a\" and \"a-5\" parse 'a' as 10)."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/kstrtox.c"], "summary": "Fixed inverted leading-'0' check in _parse_integer_fixup_radix so auto-detected base is 10 for non-zero-prefixed numbers (not octal), restoring parsing of digits 8/9 in get_option/get_options."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In unescape_octal(), the no-op expression `num << 3` discarded the shift so multi-digit octal escapes were computed wrongly; changed it to `num <<= 3`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "unescape_hex() decremented the source pointer after matching 'x' instead of advancing it, so hex_to_bin() always saw the backslash and no \\xHH sequence was ever unescaped; restored the post-increment."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_passthrough() in string_escape_mem advanced the destination pointer by 2 instead of 1 per copied byte, doubling the returned length; fixed to advance by 1."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_space() decremented the output pointer (--out) after writing the backslash instead of incrementing it, so escaped whitespace characters overwrote the backslash and produced a too-short result; changed it to ++out."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_special() decremented the output pointer (--out) instead of advancing it after writing the escaped character, so ESCAPE_SPECIAL output was truncated; changed it to ++out."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_null() decremented the output pointer after writing '0' instead of incrementing it, so the \"\\\\0\" escape sequence never advanced the destination and string_escape_mem returned a wrong (too small) length; restored the ++out."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed escape_octal() in lib/string_helpers.c, which decremented the output pointer (--out) instead of incrementing it after writing the first octal digit, producing 2-byte instead of 4-byte '\\NNN' escapes and wrong output lengths."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_hex() decremented the output pointer after writing 'x' instead of incrementing it, overwriting 'x' and under-counting the escaped length by one byte per hex-escaped character; changed `--out` to `++out`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option(), the negative-number path decremented the cursor (--cur) instead of skipping the leading '-' (++cur), so negative values like \"-3\" never parsed; restored ++cur."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In lib/cmdline.c, get_option now advances past a leading '-' (++cur instead of --cur) so negative numbers parse, and get_range fills the output array forward (*pint++) instead of backward."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "get_option() decremented the cursor (--cur) instead of advancing past the leading '-' (++cur) when parsing negative numbers, so strings like \"-3,...\" parsed garbage before the buffer and negative values were never read."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option(), the negative-number branch decremented the cursor (--cur) instead of skipping past the '-' (++cur), so values like \"-3\" were never parsed; restored ++cur."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed string_get_size decrementing the unit exponent (i--) instead of incrementing when reducing a large size, and fixed string_escape_mem reading the source buffer backwards (*src--) instead of forwards (*src++)."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed inverted check in string_unescape() so escape sequences are processed when a character follows the backslash (src[1] != '\\0') instead of never."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In lib/string_helpers.c, fixed string_get_size decrementing instead of incrementing the exponent while reducing size (producing bogus 'UNK' units), and fixed string_unescape's inverted check (src[1] == '\\0' instead of != '\\0') that prevented any escape sequence from being processed."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed string_get_size decrementing instead of incrementing the exponent when reducing a large size (yielding a negative index and 'UNK'), and fixed escape_passthrough advancing the output pointer by 2 instead of 1 (doubling escaped output length)."}
{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() walked s1 backwards (*s1--) instead of forwards; changed to *s1++ so both strings advance together."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "Restored the tail-length mask in __siphash_aligned and __hsiphash_aligned from `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)` back to `len & (sizeof(u64) - 1)`, so odd leftover byte counts are no longer dropped from the final block."}
